source_text:
τρί. Δεκτοὶ γὰρ οὐχ ἑτέρως ἐσμὲν, πλὴν ὅτι διὰ μόνου Χριστοῦ.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης.
{ΚΥΡ.} Καὶ ταυτὶ μὲν ἡμῖν ὡς ἔν γε τοῖς Σάββασι καὶ νεομηνίαις τὰ ἱερουργούμενα· «Ἐν δέ γε μηνὶ τῷ ἑβδόμῳ,» φησὶ, «μιᾷ τοῦ μηνὸς, ἐπίκλητος ἁγία ἔσται ὑμῖν. Πᾶν ἔργον λατρευτὸν οὐ ποιήσετε. Ἡμέρα σημασίας ἔσται ὑμῖν. Καὶ ποιήσετε ὁλοκαυτώματα εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ, μόσχον ἕνα ἐκ βοῶν, καὶ κριὸν ἕνα, ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους ἑπτὰ ἀμώμους.» Καὶ τρία μὲν δέκατα σεμιδάλεως ἐπὶ τῷ μόσχῳ, δύο δὲ αὖ ἐπὶ τῷ κριῷ, καὶ ἓν ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν ἀμνῶν, ἀναλόγως ἑπομένων καὶ τῶν ἐπιχεομένων, ἐλαίου τέ φημι καὶ οἴνου. Ἐν ἡμίσει γὰρ δὴ τοῦ παρ' Ἑβραίοις ἲν, καὶ ἐν τρίτῳ τε καὶ ἐν τετάρτῳ ταυτί. Τίς δ' ἂν νοοῖτο τῆς ἑορτῆς ἡ δύναμις, ὑπέφηνεν εἰπών· «Ἡμέρα σημασίας ἔσται ὑμῖν.» Σημαίνει γὰρ ἡμῖν τὴν ἐσχάτην σάλπιγγα, τὴν διὰ τῆς ἀγγέλου φωνῆς, ὑφ' ᾗ δὴ πάντες ἀναστήσονται οἱ νεκροὶ, καὶ ἐγερθήσονται οἱ ἐν τοῖς μνημείοις, καθάπερ ἤδη προείπομεν. Προστέταχε δὲ καὶ ἐν τῇ δεκάτῃ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μηνὸς, καθ' ἢν ἡ νηστεία, τῶν σαρκικῶν ἐπιθυμιῶν, τὴν νέκρωσιν, καὶ τὴν ἐκ τῶν ἐπιγείων παθῶν ἀποφοίτησιν ἐφ' ἑαυτῇ καταγράφουσα, τὴν αὐτὴν θυσίαν ἀποπεραίνεσθαι δεῖν κατὰ τὸν ἴσον τῇ πρώτῃ τρόπον, καὶ ὅπως ἂν ἔχοι τῶν δρωμένων ἡ δύναμις κατά γε τὸν πρέποντα ταῖς θεωρίαις λόγον, διαρκῶς εἰρήκαμεν.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Μεμνήσομαι.
{ΚΥΡ.} Θεσμοθετεῖ δὲ αὖ καὶ τίνες ἂν γένοιντο πρὸς ἡμῶν θυσίαι τῇ Σκηνοπηγίᾳ πρέπουσαι, καὶ φησί· «Καὶ τῇ πεντεκαιδεκάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ μηνὸς τοῦ ἑβδόμου τοῦ ἐπικληθέντος ἁγία ἔσται ὑμῖν. Πᾶν ἔργον λατρευτὸν οὐ ποιήσετε. Καὶ ἑορτάσετε αὐτὴν ἑορτὴν Κυρίῳ ἑπτὰ ἡμέρας, καὶ προσάξετε ὁλοκαυτώματα κάρπωμα τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας, τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ πρώτῃ μόσχους ἐκ βοῶν τρεῖς καὶ δέκα, κριοὺς δύο, ἀμνοὺς ἐνιαυσίους δεκατέσσαρας Ἄμωμοι ἔσονται. Αἱ θυσίαι αὐτῶν σεμίδαλις ἀναπεποιημένη ἐν ἐλαίῳ. Τρία δέκατα τῷ μόσχῳ τῷ ἑνὶ, ἐπὶ τοῖς τρισκαίδεκα μόσχοις, καὶ δύο δέκατα τῷ κριῷ τῷ ἑνὶ, ἐπὶ τοὺς δύο κριούς. Δέκατον δέκατον τῷ ἀμνῷ τῷ ἑνὶ, ἐπὶ τοὺς τέσσαρας καὶ δέκα ἀμνοὺς, καὶ χίμαρον ἐξ αἰγῶν ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας, πλὴν τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως τῆς διαπαντὸς, αἱ θυσίαι αὐτῶν καὶ αἱ σπονδαὶ αὐτῶν.» Εἶτα καθ' ἡμέραν ἑνὸς ὑπεξαιρομένου μόσχου, τὰ τῆς θυσίας ἐν ἴσῳ τρόπῳ τε καὶ μέτρῳ. Δύο γὰρ οἱ κριοὶ, καὶ ἀμνοὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ χίμαρος εἷς. Καὶ γοῦν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ δευτέρᾳ μόσχοι προσεκομίζοντο δύο καὶ δέκα· ἕνδεκα δὲ τῇ τρίτῃ, τῇ δὲ τετάρτῃ δέκα· καὶ ἐννέα τῇ πέμπτῃ, ὀκτὼ τῇ ἕκτῃ, καὶ ἑπτὰ κατὰ τὴν ἑβδόμην. Συνίης οὖν ὅτι καθ' ἑκάστην, ἡμέραν ὁ τῶν μόσχων ἀριθμὸς ἐν ὑφέσει μόνος, ἐν ἴσῳ γε μὴν ὅ τε τῶν κριῶν, καὶ μὲν καὶ ὁ τῶν ἀμνῶν τὰ τῆς σεμιδάλεως, καὶ τῶν ἐκχεομένων.
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ τί τὸ χρῆμα, ὦ τᾶν; ἀνθ' ὅτου δὲ δὴ μόσχοι μὲν ἐν ἀρχαῖς τρισκαίδεκα, ἐν ὑφέσει δὲ
pass_a_gloss: (to the Fa)ther. For we are acceptable not otherwise except that through Christ alone. PALL.: Best you said. CYR.: And these things then for us as on the Sabbaths and new moons are the things sacrificed. 'And in the seventh month,' he says, 'on one of the month, a holy convocation will be for you. Every work of service you will not do. A day of signaling it will be for you. And you will do whole burnt offerings for an odor of fragrance to the Lord, one calf from cattle, and one ram, lambs a year old seven unblemished.' And three tenths of fine flour upon the calf, and two again upon the ram, and one upon each of the lambs, the things poured on also following proportionally, oil I say and wine. For in half of the hin among the Hebrews, and in a third and in a fourth these. And what the power of the feast would be understood, he hinted, saying: 'A day of signaling it will be for you.' For it signals to us the last trumpet, the one through the voice of the angel, under which all the dead will rise, and those in the tombs will be raised, just as we already said before. And he ordered also on the tenth of the same month, on which is the fast, inscribing on itself the deadening of the fleshly desires and the departure from the earthly passions, that the same sacrifice must be completed according to the equal way to the first; and how the power of the things done would hold according to the account befitting the contemplations, we have said sufficiently. PALL.: I will remember. CYR.: And he legislates again also what sacrifices by us would be fitting to the Tent-pitching, and he says: 'And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the one so called, it will be holy for you. Every work of service you will not do. And you will feast it a feast to the Lord seven days, and you will bring whole burnt offerings, an offering to the Lord for an odor of fragrance; on the first day calves from cattle three and ten, rams two, lambs a year old fourteen; unblemished they will be. Their sacrifices fine flour mixed in oil. Three tenths for the one calf, upon the thirteen calves, and two tenths for the one ram, upon the two rams. A tenth, a tenth for the one lamb, upon the fourteen lambs, and one he-goat from goats concerning sin, besides the whole burnt offering throughout all, their sacrifices and their libations.' Then, one calf being withdrawn each day, the things of the sacrifice in equal way and measure. For two the rams, and lambs fourteen, and one he-goat. And so on the second day calves were brought twelve; eleven on the third, and on the fourth ten; and nine on the fifth, eight on the sixth, and seven on the seventh. You understand then that each day the number of the calves alone is in decrease, but in equality both that of the rams, and also that of the lambs, the things of the fine flour and of the things poured out. PALL.: And what is the matter, my good man? Instead of what then were calves at the beginnings thirteen, and in decrease (continues).
pass_b_english: Cyril: …For we are acceptable in no other way than through Christ alone.

Cyril: These, then, are the offerings for us on the sabbaths and the new moons. ‘And in the seventh month,’ it says, ‘on the first day of the month, there shall be a holy convocation for you. You shall do no work of service. It shall be for you a day of signaling. And you shall offer whole burnt offerings for a fragrant aroma to the Lord: one calf from the herd, and one ram, seven unblemished lambs a year old’ (Numbers 29:1–2). There are three tenths of fine flour for the calf, two again for the ram, and one for each of the lambs, with what is poured on, oil, I mean, and wine, following in proportion: in a half, a third and a quarter of the Hebrew hin. What the force of the feast should be taken to be, he hinted by saying, ‘It shall be for you a day of signaling.’ For it signals to us the last trumpet, sounded by the angel’s voice, at which all the dead will rise (1 Corinthians 15:52), and those in the tombs will be raised (John 5:28), as we have said before. He also commanded that on the tenth of the same month, the day of the fast, which describes in itself the putting to death of the desires of the flesh and the departure from earthly passions, the same sacrifice must be performed in the same way as on the first (Numbers 29:7–8). How the force of these rites stands, by the account that fits their contemplation, we have said sufficiently.

Cyril: He lays down, again, what sacrifices we are to offer as fitting for the feast of Tabernacles, and says: ‘And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, so called, it shall be holy for you. You shall do no work of service. And you shall keep it as a feast to the Lord seven days, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings, an offering to the Lord for a fragrant aroma: on the first day thirteen calves from the herd, two rams, fourteen lambs a year old; they shall be without blemish. Their sacrifices shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each calf, for the thirteen calves, and two tenths for each ram, for the two rams; a tenth for each lamb, for the fourteen lambs; and one male goat from the goats for sin, besides the continual whole burnt offering; their sacrifices and their drink offerings’ (Numbers 29:12–16). Then, with one calf taken away each day, the sacrifice goes on in the same manner and measure. For the rams are two, the lambs fourteen, and the goat one. And so on the second day twelve calves were brought; eleven on the third, and ten on the fourth; nine on the fifth, eight on the sixth, and seven on the seventh (Numbers 29:17–32). Do you understand, then, that each day the number of the calves alone decreases, while the number of the rams stays equal, and so too that of the lambs, and the fine flour and what is poured out?
Palladius: And what does this mean, my friend? Why were there thirteen calves at the beginning, decreasing…

choices.why: Cyril builds on the verb: the day 'signals' (σημαίνει) the last trumpet; English keeps the link.

choices.english: of the seventh month, so called, it shall be holy for you
choices.why: Cyril's text differs from the LXX ('ἐπίκλητος ἁγία', a holy convocation); rendered as printed.
